engine.title: Scientific engine
engine.methodsNone: No scientific method in this version
engine.unavailable: Could not communicate with the calculation engine.

home.title: What would you like to do?

plan.title: Plan an experiment
plan.text: Define factors and responses and generate the run matrix.
plan.example: E.g. factors and limits → collection matrix.

analyze.title: Analyze existing data
analyze.text: Type or paste results you have already measured and summarize them.
analyze.example: E.g. CSV or worksheet → summaries and models.

compare.title: Compare treatments
compare.text: Compare the means of conditions or treatments.
compare.example: E.g. treatments and responses → comparisons and intervals.

availability.limited: Unavailable in this engine: the {{missing}} part is not registered in the loaded build. Update the app or reload the page.

home.recentEmpty: No recent projects. Open a file or try an example.
home.readyHint: Ready: use “Next” to continue with the chosen option.
home.recentHint: Or continue a project you already saved.

blocked.variables: Add at least one named response.
blocked.data: Enter at least one observation with a value and fix the cells with errors.

variables.title: Factors and responses
variables.intro: Factors are the conditions you vary or compare (for example, temperature or enzyme type). Responses are what you measure. You define the names and units.
variables.name: Name
variables.levelsHelp: Separate with semicolons, in the order you want. Empty: uses the labels found in the data, in alphabetical order.
variables.noFactors: No factors. You can summarize a response without factors.
variables.noResponses: No responses. Add at least one.
variables.planKindHelp: For planning, new factors start as numeric. Use categorical for treatments without a numeric scale. Discrete levels can also be numeric.
variables.compareKindHelp: For treatment comparisons, new factors start as categorical. Choose numeric for a measured quantity; this choice guides design and analysis options.

data.title: Data
data.intro: Type or paste the observations (from Excel, for example). Empty cells are missing data; numbers accept a dot or comma as the decimal separator.
data.caption: Observations table
data.showUnitHelp: Identifies the same unit across repeated observations. Names with spaces or accents are preserved; distinct units receive distinct internal identifiers.
data.empty: No observations yet. Add a row or paste your data.
data.pasteNote: Tip: click a cell and paste (Ctrl+V). Several values copied from Excel fill the following cells.
data.pasteIgnored: {{count}} pasted column(s) beyond the last table column were ignored.
data.errorsSummary: {{count}} cell(s) with errors. Fix them before analyzing.
data.needColumns: Add factors and responses in the previous step to create the columns.
data.conditionsLocked: Design conditions are protected. Fill the response columns.
data.conditionsUnlocked: Condition editing enabled; review the matrix before analyzing.
data.confirmConditions: Editing conditions may make the data differ from the generated design. Enable editing?
data.missingNote: Empty cells represent missing data; invalid values are marked as errors.
data.showTimeHelp: Identifies when a unit was measured. The covariance structure uses this information; time does not automatically replace a factor.

analysis.title: Analysis: descriptive summary
analysis.intro: Summarizes the chosen response with count, missing, mean, variance, standard deviation, minimum and maximum. This describes the data; it is not a comparison test.
analysis.groupByHelp: Check factors to summarize each combination of levels separately.

compare.title: Analysis: treatment comparison
compare.intro: Compares the means of a factor's levels: one-way ANOVA (completely randomised design), Tukey comparisons (Tukey–Kramer when group sizes differ) and comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
compare.factorHelp: Each level of the factor forms a group. Rows without a response or without a level are left out and reported.
compare.alphaHelp: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
compare.needFactor: Add a factor (for example, the condition being tested) to define the groups.
compare.needLevels: Enter the factor levels in the variables step or type the data: at least two groups are required.

introFor.tukey: Compares the means of a factor's levels: one-way ANOVA (completely randomized design), Tukey comparisons (Tukey–Kramer when group sizes differ) and comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.gamesHowell: Compares the means of a factor's levels without assuming equal variances: Welch ANOVA and Games–Howell comparisons, with comparison letters. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.dunnett: Compares each treatment with a control (Dunnett), starting from the one-way ANOVA. Choose the control level. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.bonferroni: Compares the means of a factor's levels with pairwise t tests adjusted by Bonferroni, starting from the one-way ANOVA. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.holm: Compares the means of a factor's levels with pairwise t tests adjusted by Holm, starting from the one-way ANOVA. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.kruskalDunn: Compares the groups without assuming normality: Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn comparisons. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.
introFor.factorial: Fits the ANOVA with several factors and/or blocks, in the model chosen below, and compares the means of each effect with the chosen multiplicity adjustment. Each row must be an independent experimental replicate.

alphaHelpFor.tukey: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.gamesHowell: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.dunnett: Applies to the family of comparisons of each treatment with the control (simultaneous confidence 1 − α).
alphaHelpFor.bonferroni: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons, with the Bonferroni adjustment.
alphaHelpFor.holm: Applies to the family of all pairwise comparisons, with the Holm adjustment.
alphaHelpFor.kruskalDunn: Applies to the global test and to the family of Dunn pairwise comparisons.
alphaHelpFor.factorial: Applies to the ANOVA and to the family of comparisons of each effect.

design.title: Analysis: two-level design
design.intro: Estimates effects and coefficients on the coded scale (−1, +1), with Pareto, main effects, interactions and observed vs predicted. Without error degrees of freedom only Lenth's method flags active effects, and it is labelled as such.
design.needDesign: Generate the design in the data step (or open a project that contains it).
design.modelHelp: Terms aliased with each other (fractional designs) appear as not estimable.
design.curvatureUnavailable: The design has no centre points.

surface.title: Analysis: response surface
surface.intro: Fits the chosen terms (up to second order) on the coded scale and displays ANOVA, lack of fit, the equation and response surface.
surface.needFactors: Add at least one quantitative factor to fit the model.
surface.modelHelp: Terms can be removed manually; the app never drops terms on its own. Quadratic terms and interactions without the matching main effect are flagged.
surface.asSurfaceHelp: Use for custom or imported matrices with quantitative factors; the coded scale uses the lowest and highest value of each factor.
surface.needDesign: Generate the design in the data step.

help.tukey: Default: all pairs, assuming equal variances.
help.gamesHowell: Use when groups have very different variances or sizes.
help.dunnett: Use when only each treatment against the control matters.
help.bonferroni: All pairs with pooled variance; conservative.
help.kruskalDunn: Use when data are not normally distributed or are ordinal.

method.blockHelp: The block enters as an additive effect (no interaction) and removes between-block variation from the error.
method.ssHelp: With balanced data the three types agree; with unbalanced data, type III tests each term after all others and type II respects model hierarchy.
method.contrastsHelp: Define a linear combination of one factor's means (coefficients sum to zero), for example 1; -0.5; -0.5.
method.contrastInvalid: Enter a name and {{count}} numeric coefficients (one per factor level).
method.weightSum: Weight sum = {{sum}} (must be zero; at least one weight must be nonzero).
method.contrastWeightsInvalid: Weights must sum to zero, with at least one nonzero weight.

analysis.mixtureInterim: Mixture results are available in Analysis and Results during this session. Project persistence will be integrated in ET22; fit again after reopening.
analysis.dependent: Repeated measures on the same unit
analysis.summaryText: {{response}} will be analyzed using {{method}}, under model {{model}}.
analysis.recordSummaryText: Response {{response}} was analyzed using {{method}} under model {{model}}.

project.name: Project name
project.saveBrowserHelp: In the browser, saving downloads the .desvtag file; the previous file is not replaced.
project.confirmDiscard: There are changes not saved to a file. Continue and lose those changes?
project.failed: The operation could not be completed. The open project was not changed.
project.invalidExtension: Choose a filename with the .desvtag extension.
project.migrated: File from format version {{from}}, upgraded in memory; the original file was not changed.

status.title: Saving status
status.unsaved: Changes not saved to a file
status.recoveryPending: waiting for a 2 s pause in editing…
status.recoveryError: unavailable in this browser; your changes are not protected
status.recoveryNote: It stays in this browser; it is not an external backup.

recovery.title: Unsaved session found
recovery.text: There is a session with unsaved changes, kept in this browser at {{time}}. Restore it?

history.title: Version history
history.intro: Each version is a snapshot of the data created when importing, analyzing, saving or restoring. Nothing is deleted automatically.
history.restoreNote: Restoring creates a new version; the current one stays in the history.

import.title: Import data
import.intro: Review the preview, choose each column's role and confirm. The current data stays in the version history.
import.encodingFallback: The file was not valid UTF-8; it was read as Windows-1252. Check the accents in the preview.
import.header: The first row contains the column names
import.replaceNote: The current data of this experiment will be replaced; it stays in the version history.
import.unitHelp: Rows with the same experimental unit are repeated measurements of that unit, not independent replicates.
import.failed: The file could not be read:
import.formulaNote: Spreadsheets: only stored values are read; formulas are never executed.
import.nothing: Nothing to import: choose at least one column as a factor or response.

fill.title: Fill in the design responses
fill.intro: This file has the factors and responses of this experiment (for example, the collection sheet exported from the run matrix). Each line is matched to the run with the same levels (or the same unit) and only the responses are written; the design and the factors stay as they are.
fill.modeLegend: What to do with the file
fill.modeFill: Fill in only the responses of the current experiment (recommended)
fill.modeReplace: Replace all data with this file
fill.summary: {{filled}} response value(s) will be written; {{empty}} blank cell(s) in the file are left as they are.
fill.replacing: {{count}} value(s) already entered will be replaced; the previous state stays in the version history.
fill.unmatched: {{count}} line(s) of the file match no run (levels differ from the planned ones, or the run was already used) and will not be written. Lines: {{lines}}.
fill.invalid: {{count}} response cell(s) are not numbers and must be fixed in the file. Lines: {{lines}}.
fill.rowsWithoutLine: {{count}} run(s) of the experiment have no line in the file and stay as they are.
fill.keeps: Factors, run order and design do not change.

import.startHere: You can start from a file; factors and responses will be defined in column mapping.

design.title: Experiment design
design.intro: Generates the two-level run matrix for factor screening. Each factor must be quantitative, with a low and a high level. The run count is shown before generating.
design.needFactors: Add at least two quantitative factors (with a name) in the previous step.
design.categoricalIgnored: Categorical factors are not part of a two-level design: {{names}}.
design.levelsInvalid: The low level must be smaller than the high level (numbers).
design.budgetHelp: Counts the basic design only, without replicates or centre points.
design.replicatesHelp: Each repetition redoes every run. They are experimental replicates only if each run is a new independent preparation.
design.centerHelp: They allow testing for curvature. A single centre point gives no error estimate.
design.seedHelp: The same seed gives the same order on Windows and in the browser.
design.countError: The runs could not be counted.
design.confirmReplace: Replace the current runs with the new matrix? The current data stay in the version history.
design.generated: Design generated: {{total}} runs. Fill in the responses in the grid below.

matrix.title: Run matrix
matrix.failed: The matrix could not be exported.

properties.title: Properties
properties.aliasesHelp: Effects on the same line cannot be separated by this design: what is estimated is their sum.
properties.pbPartial: Plackett–Burman: main effects are partially aliased with two-factor interactions (maximum absolute correlation {{value}}).
properties.dummy: {{count}} dummy columns (contrasts not used by factors): they remain as error degrees of freedom.
properties.axial: Central composite: α = {{alpha}}; {{factorial}} factorial points, {{axial}} axial and {{center}} centre points.

surface.intro: Central composite and Box–Behnken designs estimate curvature (quadratic terms). Use them after screening, with the factors that matter. Centre points are needed to estimate pure error.
surface.custom: Central composite with a given α
surface.inscribed: Inscribed: axial points sit at the stated levels and the factorial part inside them
surface.inscribedHelp: Circumscribed (default): the factorial part sits at the stated levels and the axial points beyond them, at ±α.
surface.cubeGeneratorsHelp: Comma-separated generators, for example E=ABCD. Empty: full factorial.
surface.centerSuggested: Centre points set to 5 (needed for pure error).
surface.axialPreview: Axial distance α = {{alpha}}. Review the ranges below: in a circumscribed composite design, axial runs may exceed the low and high cube limits.

mode.rcbd: One categorical factor in blocks (randomized RCBD)

crd.intro: Completely randomized design: one factor with several treatments (levels), the same number of independent experimental units in each, and a run order drawn with a recorded seed.
crd.needFactor: Add a named categorical factor in the previous step to plan the CRD.
crd.levelsHelp: Separate with semicolons or line breaks, for example: Control; pH 5; pH 7. The levels are stored on the factor.
crd.replicatesHelp: Each unit is an independent preparation or sample. Measuring the same sample several times does not create a new unit.
crd.unitNote: Each run gets an experimental-unit identifier (for example T2-R3: level 2, unit 3).

rcbd.intro: Randomized complete block design: each block (day, batch, operator…) gets every treatment once, in an order drawn within the block. Between-block variation is removed from the error.
rcbd.needFactors: Add two named categorical factors in the previous step: one for the treatments and one for the blocks.
rcbd.randomize: Randomize the order within each block
rcbd.unitNote: Each run gets a unit identifier (for example B2-T3: block 2, treatment 3). The analysis uses the block as an additive effect.

design.collectionNote: Collection sheet: the exported file has an empty column for each response. Fill it in at the lab and import the same file with “Import file”: only the responses are written, into the matching runs.

mixed.title: Mixed-levels factorial
mixed.intro: Combines every level of two or more factors with different numbers of levels (for example 3 strains × 2 pH values × 4 agitation speeds), with replicates and a run order drawn with a recorded seed. The analysis is the multi-factor ANOVA, with marginal means and contrasts.
mixed.needFactors: In the previous step, add at least two named factors with two or more levels typed in the «Levels» field.
mixed.levelsHelp: Each factor's levels are stored on the factor itself, separated by semicolons or line breaks. Numeric factors enter as named levels.
mixed.matrix: Run order of the mixed-levels factorial

mixture.boundedHelp: Vertices define the region. Two subdivisions per edge include the midpoints. Extra center points repeat the mean of the vertex compositions.
mixture.extremeVertices: Vertices and edges of the bounded region
mixture.numericBounds: Enter valid numeric bounds for the components.
mixture.regionSummary: The region has {{vertices}} vertices, {{edges}} edges and dimension {{dimension}}.
mixture.title: Mixture design
mixture.intro: Components are proportions that sum to 1. Choose lattice or centroid for the simplex, or vertices and edges for a region with upper bounds. Lower bounds define the transformation to pseudo-components.
mixture.needFactors: In the previous step, add at least two named numeric factors: each is the proportion of one mixture component.
mixture.lowerHelp: The lower bounds must sum to less than 1. Leave 0 when there is no bound.

warn.no_pure_error: Without replicates or extra center points there is no pure error to test lack of fit.

optimal.title: D- and I-optimal design
optimal.intro: Chooses, from a grid of candidates inside your constraints, the runs that best estimate the model: D maximizes the information on the coefficients; I minimizes the average prediction variance over the region. Useful for irregular regions, a fixed number of runs and for augmenting runs already done.
optimal.needFactors: Add at least one numeric or categorical factor.
optimal.needRanges: Enter the low and high limits (numbers) of every chosen factor.
optimal.levels: Levels per factor in the grid
optimal.constraintEquation: The sum of coefficient × value must be less than or equal to the limit, in real units.
optimal.constraintHelp: Example: coefficients 1 and 1 with limit 40 mean factor 1 + factor 2 ≤ 40. Leave blank the coefficient of a factor that does not take part.
optimal.augment: Augment: preserve {{count}} completed runs (complete selected factors and at least one response)
optimal.randomize: Randomize the run order of the new runs
optimal.summary: {{runs}} runs chosen from {{candidates}} candidates; the best value was reached in {{reached}} of {{starts}} starts.
optimal.searchStarts: Starts attempted ({{attempted}}), with a result ({{succeeded}}), without a result ({{failed}}) and reaching the pass limit ({{limited}}).
optimal.searchWork: Singular random starts ({{singular}}), recovery attempts ({{recoveries}}), exchanges evaluated ({{evaluations}}) and passes ({{passes}}).

stops.noImprovingExchange: The selected design had no exchange improving the criterion within the adopted tolerance.
stops.passLimit: The selected design reached its pass limit. An improving exchange may remain.
stops.workLimit: The selected design's scan reached the work budget. An improving exchange may remain.
stops.singular: Search found no full-rank information matrix.

optimal.noGlobal: The search compares local exchanges. A better design may exist in the candidate region.
optimal.apply: Use this design in the data
optimal.applied: {{count}} new runs went to the data grid; the analysis will be a response surface (choose the model terms in the result).
optimal.excluded: Unselected factors will be left out of the matrix: {{names}}.
optimal.confirmEmpty: These columns will be empty in the data grid: {{names}}. You will have to fill them in before analyzing. Use the design anyway?
optimal.appliedEmpty: Fill in the columns that were left empty in the grid: {{names}}.
optimal.invalidConfiguration: Check ranges and constraints: enter numbers without empty fields or invalid text.

categories.title: Categorical treatment factors
categories.coding: Categories use sum contrasts, with one fewer parameter than their level count. Interactions include numeric × categorical and categorical × categorical terms. Squares apply only to numeric factors.
categories.needLevels: Declare at least two levels in the variables or fill in levels in the data grid.
categories.allCombinations: Every combination of the selected levels is crossed with the admissible numeric region.
categories.allowedOnly: Only listed combinations enter the region. Numeric linear constraints apply to every permitted combination.
categories.empty: Add at least one combination or disable the restriction.
categories.domainReset: The factor selection changed. The region now includes all combinations; review permitted combinations before searching.
categories.modelHelp: The model uses sum contrasts for categories and blocks. D and A depend on this coding; I and G use the uniform distribution over all admissible candidates and declared blocks.
categories.spatialTuple: Categorical combination for the spatial figure
categories.noNumericMap: This design contains categories only. The distribution and labelled source table describe its precision; there are no numeric axes for a spatial map.
categories.analysisHelp: The fit uses the same coding, categorical factors, interactions and numeric terms as the design, including declared blocks. Errors are independent and homoscedastic. This is not a surface that omits categories.
categories.measure: Every permitted categorical combination is included, with equal weight per complete condition.
categories.profileSource: {{runs}} runs · {{parameters}} parameters · {{candidates}} candidate conditions (numeric and categorical) · profile v{{version}}.

design.pbTwoFactors: With two factors, compare the total with the full factorial: Plackett–Burman may increase the run count without adding interaction separation.

requirements.factorial: Requires at least 2 numeric factors with low and high limits.
requirements.crd: Requires one factor and at least 2 discrete levels, numeric or categorical.
requirements.rcbd: Requires treatment and block factors with defined levels.
requirements.mixed: Requires at least 2 factors with 2 or more discrete levels each.
requirements.mixture: Requires at least 2 numeric components; proportions sum to 1.
requirements.optimal: Uses numeric and/or categorical factors. Each categorical factor needs at least two levels.

optimization.legacyDesirability: This saved result used an earlier formula that could miscalculate desirability at extreme limits. Run the optimization again before using the candidates.
optimization.title: Desirability optimization
optimization.intro: Set the goal of each response (preference) and, if needed, mandatory limits. The search uses the second-order models fitted to your data, starts from many points and presents candidates with predictions and intervals. It does not guarantee the global optimum: confirm the candidates with new runs.
optimization.stale: The data or the setup changed since this search: run it again to refresh the candidates.
optimization.convergence: Search: {{starts}} starts (seed {{seed}}); {{converged}} converged by tolerance; {{feasible}} ended at feasible points; {{distinct}} distinct solution(s); the best was found by {{best}} starts.

status.found: Feasible candidates with positive desirability were found.
status.onlyZeroDesirability: The search found only candidates with zero overall desirability. This does not establish that the goals are impossible throughout the region.
status.infeasible: The search found no candidate satisfying the mandatory limits.

goals.title: Response goals
goals.help: Preferences (goal and importance) are combined into a global desirability; mandatory limits (minimum or maximum predicted value) remove points and are not traded off against other responses.
goals.importanceHelp: Relative weight in the global desirability (default 1).
goals.limitHelp: Leave empty if there is no limit.

goal.targetHelp: Desirability is 1 from (or up to) this value.
goal.shapeHelp: 1 = linear; greater than 1 demands getting closer to the target.

domain.title: Search domain
domain.region: Experimental region (default): the factor ranges actually run, no extrapolation
domain.extended: Extend the factor limits (extrapolation, by explicit choice)
domain.help: Outside the experimental region the model has not been tested: candidates outside it are marked as extrapolation.

search.title: Advanced search options
search.startsHelp: More starts give more confidence that the best candidate is not a local optimum (1 to 5000).
search.seedHelp: The same seed gives the same candidates.

run.cancelled: Search cancelled; the previous results were kept.
run.needResponse: Include at least one response in the optimization.

candidates.caption: Candidates (real conditions and, in parentheses, coded)

tradeoffs.title: Trade-offs between responses
tradeoffs.help: Best desirability each response would reach alone (same constraints). In the candidates, the number in parentheses is how much individual desirability was given up.

view.heading: Global desirability over two factors
view.legacy: This saved result predates the archived model coefficients. Rebuilding the figure fits the models from the linked revision.
view.title: Global desirability
view.description: Global desirability as a function of two factors, with the others fixed at the best candidate's conditions.
view.reading: Lines: global desirability; darker = more desirable.
view.points: Numbers: candidates projected onto the two axes. Other factors in the map are fixed at the first candidate’s conditions.
view.sameAxis: Choose different factors on the two axes.

confirmation.title: Confirmation runs
confirmation.intro: Choose candidates and replicates: the app creates a new experiment, linked to this one, with the conditions rounded to 5 significant digits and the predictions stored to compare with what is observed.

check.title: Check against the predictions
check.help: Predictions stored with the proposal, with a {{level}}% prediction interval.
check.note: A value inside the interval is compatible with the model; outside it, the model may not describe these conditions well. With few runs the conclusion is limited.
check.originHelp: This is the saved analysis that generated the confirmation. The source experiment may have received later edits.

decision.criterionHelp: The search combines desirabilities through a weighted geometric mean and requires every mandatory limit to be satisfied. Desirability 1 already meets the objective; increasing a response beyond that threshold does not increase the criterion.
decision.shown: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} distinct solutions clustered by the engine.
decision.order: Ordered by global desirability, highest first. The number identifies a candidate and does not break ties by predicted response.
decision.ties: {{count}} displayed candidates have the same desirability {{value}}. Choose using the predicted response, uncertainty and operating conditions.
decision.invalidNumber: Enter a valid number in required fields; leave optional limits blank to impose no limit.

summary.maximize: Below {{low}}, d = 0; at {{target}} or above, d = 1.
summary.minimize: Up to {{target}}, d = 1; at {{high}} or above, d = 0.
summary.target: At the target {{target}}, d = 1; at the limits {{low}} and {{high}}, d = 0.
summary.range: Between {{low}} and {{high}}, d = 1; outside that range, d = 0.

update.current: You already have the latest version.
update.failed: Could not check right now (no internet or service unavailable).
update.safe: The update is installed only if its signature matches the app's key. Your projects are your own files and are not changed.
update.notes: What is new in this version

channelHelp.experimental: Receives every published version, including the 0.x series. It is the only channel until version 1.0.0 exists.
channelHelp.stable: Receives stable versions only (from 1.0.0). Until then this channel has no versions and the check will report that it could not verify.

analysis.optimIntervals: Mean confidence intervals and prediction intervals for a new observation at {{level}}% confidence, under the fitted model.
analysis.optimPointDomain: The region admits a single composition; there are no free search directions.
analysis.optimHelp: Include up to eight responses. Each response is fitted separately with the selected Scheffe model. The search respects the sum of 1 and the component bounds declared in the design.
analysis.optimBudget: Use 1 to 128 starts. The local search allows up to 100,000 combined evaluations and may return candidates with a budget warning. More starts do not prove a global optimum.
analysis.optimInvalid: Check these fields or observations before calculating: {{fields}}.
analysis.fitOptimize: Fit models and optimize the mixture
analysis.optimNoGlobalClaim: The search is local and does not prove a global optimum. Desirability evaluates predictions; confirm the candidate with new runs.
analysis.optimWork: {{executed}} of {{requested}} starts executed; {{converged}} by tolerance, {{limited}} at a limit; {{evaluations}} evaluations.
analysis.optimHighlight: Diamond: best candidate found by the desirability search.
analysis.legacyFixedWarning: Result predates the correction for fixed components. Review the fit before using its predictions.
analysis.coxEnable: Include a Cox trace in the result
analysis.coxHelp: Enter fractions from 0 to 1 that sum to 1 and respect the mixture bounds. Each curve varies one component while keeping the ratios between all others.
analysis.coxNumericReference: Enter a valid number for every reference fraction.
analysis.coxXLabel: Change in real fraction from the reference (Δx)
analysis.coxNote: Zero marks the reference blend. Each line varies the named component while keeping the ratios between the others. Only feasible paths and estimable predictions are shown; gaps are not joined.
analysis.coxNoPredictions: No estimable predictions are available to draw the requested traces. Check model rank and data.
analysis.legacyPredictionWarning: This rank-deficient result comes from an earlier method version. Its grid may contain non-estimable predictions and requires verification.
analysis.boundedDomain: Predictions and colored cells stay within the mixture bounds. The outline marks the declared region; only cells with estimable predictions are colored.
analysis.boundedLegend: Dashed line marks the region bounds. Only cells with valid predictions are colored.
analysis.title: Mixture analysis (Scheffé models)
analysis.intro: Fits the chosen model without an intercept on the pseudo-components. The ANOVA uses the mean-centered total sum of squares. The result is computed on request and is not stored in the project.
analysis.note: No intercept: the linear terms already carry the average level. Coefficients are in pseudo-components; predictions are valid only inside the design region.
analysis.badCells: Some responses are not numbers in rows {{rows}}.
analysis.pseudoAxes: Pseudocomponent fractions (0–1), after removing lower bounds; circles: measured runs. Colors: predicted response.
analysis.realAxes: Component fractions (0–1); circles: measured runs. Colors: predicted response.
analysis.optimMissingResponse: Response {{id}} was removed from the experiment. Remove this goal before optimizing again.

repeated.title: Repeated measures, paired data and mixed models
repeated.intro: For data that are not independent: the same unit measured under two conditions (paired) or several times (repeated measures, lots, days). Both tools use the «Unit» column of the data grid. Results are computed on request and are not stored in the project.
repeated.needUnits: No row has an experimental unit. Show the «Unit» column and fill it in (for example, the subject or lot identifier).
repeated.showUnitColumn: Show the «Unit» column in the grid

paired.title: Paired comparison (two conditions)
paired.needTwoLevels: Needs a categorical factor with exactly two levels in the data.
paired.noPairs: No unit has both conditions with a response. Check the “Experimental unit” chosen above and that each unit was measured in both conditions.
paired.incomplete: Units left out because they have only one of the conditions: {{units}}.
paired.duplicated: Units left out because they have more than one observation at the same level: {{units}}.
paired.withoutUnit: {{count}} row(s) without a unit were ignored.
paired.note: The paired t assumes roughly normal differences; Wilcoxon drops zero differences and uses mid-ranks for ties.

mixed.title: Mixed model (random intercept per unit)
mixed.boundary: The between-unit variance is zero (boundary): the model is equivalent to one without the random effect and the degrees of freedom are the residual ones.
mixed.note: REML estimation with compound symmetry (all measures of a unit share the same correlation). AR(1) and unstructured covariances are not available yet.

unit.label: Experimental unit
unit.help: The individual, batch or plot measured more than once. Choose a factor if the unit is already in it.
unit.summary: {{complete}} unit(s) with both conditions form a pair; {{incomplete}} incomplete and {{duplicated}} with a repeat in the same level are left out.
unit.sameAsPair: The experimental unit cannot be the same factor that defines the two conditions.

saturation.title: Saturation curves (Monod, Michaelis–Menten, Haldane and Hill)
saturation.intro: Choose the substrate, response and curve to fit the data. For now, this result is not saved in the project file.
saturation.needFactor: Add a numeric factor (the substrate) to fit a saturation curve.
saturation.badCells: Some values are not numbers in rows {{rows}}.
saturation.starts: {{reached}} of {{run}} starts reached the best fit.

warn.not_converged: The fit did not converge within the iteration limit: do not use these values.
warn.parameter_at_bound: A parameter ended at a (positivity) bound: the model may not suit the data.
warn.ill_conditioned: The information matrix is ill-conditioned: parameters cannot be identified separately.
warn.highly_correlated: Two parameters are correlated above 0.99: the data do not separate them (substrate range too narrow).
warn.imprecise_parameter: A standard error is more than ten times the estimate: the parameter is practically undetermined.
warn.few_degrees_of_freedom: Few degrees of freedom: the intervals are unreliable.
warn.single_start_best: Only one start reached the best fit: confirm with runs at other concentrations.

saturation.note: Wald intervals (approximation). The fit only holds inside the measured substrate range; identifying Ks and μmax needs measurements below and above Ks.
saturation.stale: This fit is for other inputs (factor, response, model or data): fit again to update it.
saturation.methodDetails: Nonlinear least squares with Levenberg–Marquardt and multiple starting values. Check convergence, parameters and intervals before interpreting the fit.
saturation.bandLabel: Band: {{level}}% CI for the predicted mean (delta method).
saturation.noBand: Confidence band unavailable; see fit warnings.

power.title: Power and sample size calculator
power.intro: Set the difference you want to detect and the expected variability to estimate power or sample size.
power.precisionNote: Sample size uses the expected standard deviation and desired two-sided half-width. A larger actual standard deviation produces a wider interval.
power.curveUnavailable: The power curve is unavailable for these assumptions.
power.note: Power holds for the σ and effect entered. If the real σ is larger, power will be lower; consider a margin.
power.stale: This result is for other values: a field changed after calculating. Calculate again to update it.
power.methodDetails: The formulas use noncentral F and t distributions. The conclusion depends on the assumed standard deviation and effect; it does not replace those assumptions with measured data.

drive.title: Google Drive (optional)
drive.intro: Save and open your projects in Google Drive. Nothing is sent until you connect, and the app only sees the «EnziTAG Optima» folder and the files it created or that you choose to open (drive.file scope).
drive.linked: Project linked to the Drive file «{{name}}».
drive.unlinked: This project is not in Drive yet: «Save to Drive» creates the file in the «EnziTAG Optima» folder.
drive.created: File «{{name}}» created in the «EnziTAG Optima» folder of your Drive.
drive.conflict: The file was changed in Drive after your last read, so it was **not overwritten**. Your work was saved as «{{copy}}» in the same folder; open both and compare before deleting either.
drive.queueAdded: Save stored on this device for retry.
drive.queueFull: The queue is full. Save a copy on your computer.
drive.queueNoMatch: No pending saves for this account.
drive.localStillWorks: Drive is optional: saving and opening files on your computer keep working as usual.
drive.waitingBrowser: Finish the authorization in the browser window that opened. The app waits up to 5 minutes.
drive.unavailable: This installation does not include the Google Drive credential for Windows. Use the web version or save to your computer.

errors.auth: Google authorization expired or was refused. Connect again.
errors.permission: No permission for this file in Drive.
errors.rateLimit: Google rate-limited the requests. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.notFound: The file was not found in Drive (deleted or outside the app's reach).
errors.cancelled: The connection was interrupted. Nothing was connected.
errors.timeout: The browser did not return the authorization in time. Try connecting again.
errors.unavailable: This installation cannot connect to Google Drive right now. The rest of the app keeps working.
errors.network: No connection to Google. Your work stays in the app; try again when you are online.
errors.unknown: Drive returned an unexpected error. Your work stays in the app.

structureHelp.compoundSymmetry: Same covariance between all measurements within a unit, with common residual variance.
structureHelp.ar1: Residual correlation decreases with temporal distance. Different units are independent; the random intercept adds common covariance.
structureHelp.unstructured: One variance per occasion and one covariance per pair. No separate random intercept, ICC or BLUP: that decomposition would not be identifiable.

mixedAdvanced.useTime: Include time / occasion and generate profiles
mixedAdvanced.timeEffect: Additional fixed effect of the time index

timeEffects.none: Do not add a time term
timeEffects.numeric: Linear slope in the time index

mixedAdvanced.orderHelp: Separate labels with semicolons in the desired order, e.g. Before; During; After. Empty uses the entered numeric values.
mixedAdvanced.timeHelp: AR(1) uses integer index differences: 0, 1, 3 preserves a missing occasion. Categorical order uses 0, 1, 2…; choose it only when that distance is appropriate.
mixedAdvanced.marginalHelp: Model means with equal weights across levels of other factors. Covariates are held at the stated reference values.
mixedAdvanced.referenceHelp: Empty uses the mean of the actual fitted cases, calculated by the engine.
mixedAdvanced.intervalAdjustment: p-values: selected procedure. Simultaneous intervals: Bonferroni within each factor, including when p-values use Holm.
mixedAdvanced.invalidSource: The selected time source no longer exists. Choose it again.
mixedAdvanced.duplicateOrder: The occasion order contains duplicate labels.
mixedAdvanced.unknownOccasion: Row {{row}}: “{{value}}” is not in the specified occasion order.
mixedAdvanced.invalidTime: Row {{row}}: “{{value}}” is not a numeric time index. Specify occasion order when using labels.
mixedAdvanced.hypothesis: Each test assesses whether the listed coefficients are jointly zero, conditional on the remaining terms and in the recorded coding. This is not a coding-invariant type III ANOVA.
mixedAdvanced.inference: Approximate Satterthwaite / Fai–Cornelius inference with observed REML information.
mixedAdvanced.profileNote: Thin lines show observations from each unit. The highlighted line shows the modeled mean at the observed conditions on each occasion. When available, bars show the CI for that mean. Gaps indicate missing observations.
mixedAdvanced.unNote: Marginal UN model: separate unit components, ICC and BLUP do not apply.
mixedAdvanced.profileLegend: Thin lines: {{units}} units; highlighted line and bars: modeled mean and CI.
mixedAdvanced.profileLegendWithoutIntervals: Thin lines: {{units}} units. Highlighted line: modeled mean. CI unavailable.

timeHelpByCovariance.compoundSymmetry: Time organizes profiles and can enter fixed effects. CS retains the same covariance between any two measurements within a unit.
timeHelpByCovariance.ar1: AR(1) uses integer index differences: 0, 1, 3 preserves a missing occasion. Categorical order uses 0, 1, 2…; choose it only when that distance is appropriate.
timeHelpByCovariance.unstructured: The order identifies occasions in the UN matrix and profiles. UN estimates each covariance freely; index distance does not impose a correlation shape.

mixedAdvanced.existingTimeEffect: {{name}} is already selected as a fixed effect. To avoid duplicate terms, do not add another time term or remove the factor from fixed effects before adding one.
mixedAdvanced.capacity: The extension accepts up to 4,096 observations, 64 fixed columns and 12 occasions for UN. A separate execution budget protects large fits; incomplete estimation or inference receives an explicit diagnostic.

saturationOptions.title: Starting values, bounds and intervals
saturationOptions.boundsHelp: Strictly positive parameters. An empty field uses the positive default lower bound or no upper bound. Starting values must lie within the bounds.
saturationOptions.profileHelp: Independent Gaussian errors with constant variance. Asymptotic likelihood-ratio intervals; unimodality is checked numerically over the examined range. The curve band remains delta/Wald.

errors.bounds: The upper bound must exceed the lower bound.
errors.inside: The starting value must lie within the bounds.

profile.title: Likelihood profile
profile.method: Asymptotic {{level}}% Gaussian likelihood-ratio CI, χ²(1) cutoff. Wald coefficient intervals are shown separately.
profile.checked: Numerically unimodal over the examined range. This does not prove global unimodality.
profile.unreliable: Inconclusive or non-unimodal profile: do not interpret as a simple interval.
profile.plotNote: The plot zooms in to LR values up to 2.5 times the cutoff. The source table preserves every examined point. Domain or search limits are not cutoff crossings.
profile.fitNote: Wald coefficient intervals and likelihood profile intervals are shown separately. The curve band is delta/Wald. The fit refers to the observed substrate range; identification requires observations on both sides of the saturation region.
profile.noCurve: Inconclusive profile: there are not enough points to plot a curve.
profile.capacity: This version accepts up to 4,096 pairs. Profiling shares an execution budget with fitting; if the search cannot finish, the app preserves the estimates and identifies unavailable limits.
profile.resourceNote: This profile search did not finish within its available budget. Completed points were preserved; no complete interval was certified.

powerAdvanced.generalIntro: Specify a fixed design and expected effects. Power depends on these assumptions and the supplied standard deviation.

intro.regression: Enter the predictors for one base-design replicate and the expected slopes. The F test assesses all slopes jointly, with an intercept.
intro.contrast: Define one comparison before collecting data: weights must sum to zero and allocation gives observations per group in each replicate.
intro.twoLevel: Choose the fitted terms and the effect to test. Each effect is the high-minus-low contrast, twice the coded coefficient.

help.regression: One condition per row, predictors separated by semicolons or tabs, without a header. You can paste from Excel. The engine includes an intercept. Each replicate repeats the entire matrix; errors are independent with equal variance. Up to 32 predictors and 4,096 base conditions, with 100,000 observations in total.
help.contrast: Means, weights and allocations use the same group order. Allocations must be positive integers; n multiplies every allocation. One contrast per calculation, without a multiple-comparison adjustment. Precision is the contrast half-width in response units.
help.twoLevel: Number factors starting at 1. Separate terms by semicolons and use * for interactions, for example 1;2;3;1*2. Supply one effect per term. The intercept is automatic and omitted terms are assumed zero. n is the number of replicates of every full-factorial combination. Up to eight factors; this does not extend to fractional or Plackett–Burman designs.

powerAdvanced.effects: Expected effects (high minus low, in term order)
powerAdvanced.hypothesisRegression: All slopes are zero, with an unrestricted intercept.
powerAdvanced.hypothesisContrast: The weighted comparison of group means is zero, using the recorded table weights.
powerAdvanced.hypothesisEffect: The {{term}} effect is zero, conditional on the fitted terms.
powerAdvanced.regressionDimensions: {{rows}} conditions per replicate and {{predictors}} predictors; intercept included.
powerAdvanced.fDetails: Noncentrality λ = {{nc}}; numerator df = {{df1}}, denominator df = {{df2}}; critical F = {{critical}}.
powerAdvanced.simulationEnable: Simulate Gaussian studies with a recorded seed
powerAdvanced.simulationHelp: Sample-size search and the curve remain analytical. Simulation checks power at the displayed n using independent Gaussian errors with constant variance. The Monte Carlo CI measures simulation error, not uncertainty in the assumptions.
powerAdvanced.simulationResultNote: {{rejections}} rejections in {{b}} studies; seed {{seed}}. The interval measures only Monte Carlo uncertainty under the recorded assumptions.
powerAdvanced.analyticLegend: Line and diamond: analytical power; diamond at the displayed n.
powerAdvanced.mcLegend: Cross and interval: simulation and 95% Wilson CI.
powerAdvanced.curveNote: Curve points are analytical engine calculations. The Monte Carlo CI appears only at the simulated n and may be smaller than the marker. The table preserves the calculated values.

execution.transportFailure: The calculation could not run. Previous results were preserved. Try again; if the problem continues, save the project and reopen the app.
execution.nativeBusy: Waiting or calculating in the background. Cancel discards this result; an existing calculation finishes before another starts.
execution.webBusy: Waiting or calculating in the background. You can cancel without interrupting saving.

blocking.title: Execution block
blocking.help: The block enters as a fixed additive effect, without interaction with quantitative factors.
blocking.referenceHelp: The equation, figures and optimization use the selected block. Replicates from different blocks are not pooled to calculate pure error.
blocking.missing: Missing block — choose a column or clear the selection
blocking.assumption: Fixed additive block model: {{name}}. Equation, predictions and intervals are conditional on block “{{reference}}”.
blocking.confirmationHelp: Confirmation retains the predictions’ reference block. A different future block may have a shift that is not included in this prediction interval.
blocking.designHelp: Completed runs stay fixed. Define the blocks and new-run counts; the search chooses conditions within each block.
blocking.fixedHelp: An existing column preserves the entered labels. To add runs to an existing block, use its name in the allocation below.
blocking.invalidAllocation: Check names and counts: 2–8 distinct blocks, completed runs with known blocks, and up to 60 total runs. Each new allocation needs 1–60 whole runs.
blocking.staleDesign: The displayed design was generated from other data or settings. Run the search again before applying another design.
blocking.criterionHelp: Model: selected polynomial + fixed additive block, without block interactions. Criteria use sum contrasts and all parameters. I uniformly averages predictions over candidates and declared blocks.
blocking.retainedRows: All {{all}} existing rows will be preserved; {{completed}} completed rows enter the search as fixed runs.
blocking.historicalPrecision: The historical table levels differ from the engine-generated levels. The original record has been preserved; check the scale and generate a new design if the matrix needs correction.

optimalVariance.title: Design prediction precision
optimalVariance.historicalDesign: Archived design from revision {{revision}}. The current table belongs to the active design.
optimalVariance.intro: Compare the conditions where the design predicts the mean with greater or lower precision. The profile uses this design’s model and candidate grid.
optimalVariance.definition: h = fᵀ(XᵀX)⁻¹f is the variance of the predicted mean divided by the error variance σ². The n·h scale uses the total run count n. It is not the variance of a future observation, which would be σ²(1+h). The calculation assumes independent errors with constant variance and does not estimate σ² from the design.
optimalVariance.precisionBlocked: The applied matrix in this older file differs from the generated levels. Check it or generate a consistent design before evaluating its precision.
optimalVariance.source: {{runs}} runs · {{parameters}} parameters · {{candidates}} spatial candidates · profile v{{version}}.
optimalVariance.applyToSave: Using this design in the data also saves the profile in the project.
optimalVariance.fdsLegend: {{count}} finite-grid evaluations in increasing order, with equal weights. {{block}}. This is not exact integration over continuous volume.
optimalVariance.codedAxes: Axes use coded coordinates z. The table and exported data also include real conditions. Factors outside the axes remain at the stated levels.
optimalVariance.spatialLegend: Numbers beside points show {{scale}}; greater intensity indicates a greater value. Only admissible candidates in this slice, without interpolating excluded regions.
optimalVariance.curveLegend: {{scale}} at admissible candidates. Segments only guide reading between the evaluated points.
optimalVariance.emptySlice: This combination of fixed factors has no admissible candidates. Choose other levels to view the slice.
optimalVariance.tableHelp: {{count}} evaluations in variance order. The preview shows up to 20 per page; export includes every row in the selected distribution, with real and coded coordinates.
